items.public_reference_text: A decision-making experiment relates evolving neural activity to choices made under uncertainty. Models may describe evidence accumulation, competing actions, or changing response thresholds. Comparing their predictions on withheld trials helps determine which aspects of behavior each model can explain.
items.initial_anchor_text: Research into decision dynamics investigates how evolving neural activity correlates with choices made under uncertain conditions. Theoretical frameworks may account for the accumulation of evidence, competing actions, or fluctuating response thresholds. Evaluating these models against withheld trial data helps identify the specific behavioral components each framework can explain.

items.public_reference_text: A locomotion controller must balance progress, stability, and energy use. Different terrain conditions can change which gait or motion strategy is effective. An evaluation should record energy expenditure over a complete task rather than comparing only a brief segment of steady motion.
items.initial_anchor_text: A locomotion controller must manage the balance between forward progress, stability, and energy consumption. Because various terrain conditions can influence the effectiveness of a specific gait or motion strategy, evaluations should document the total energy expended across an entire task rather than focusing solely on short intervals of steady-state motion.

items.public_reference_text: A phase transformation changes the structure or organization of a material under specified conditions. Studying the transition requires separating equilibrium behavior from kinetic effects caused by finite rates of heating or cooling. Repeated measurements can test how the transformation depends on the sample's previous history.
items.initial_anchor_text: Phase transformations involve structural or organizational reorganization under particular conditions. Evaluating these transitions requires researchers to distinguish between equilibrium behavior and kinetic effects resulting from finite heating or cooling rates. In addition, conducting repeated measurements can evaluate how the transformation depends upon the specific prior history of the sample.

items.public_reference_text: Quantum error correction encodes information across several physical systems so that certain errors can be detected and corrected. The code, measurement procedure, and noise assumptions must be specified together. A performance study should examine logical errors rather than only the fidelity of an individual physical operation.
items.initial_anchor_text: Quantum error correction involves encoding information across multiple physical systems to enable the detection and correction of specific errors. Such processes necessitate the simultaneous specification of the code, measurement protocols, and noise assumptions. In addition, performance assessments should emphasize logical error rates rather than exclusively considering the fidelity associated with individual physical operations.

items.public_reference_text: Single-cell assays describe variation that can disappear when measurements are averaged across a tissue. Analysis must account for incomplete sampling, technical noise, and differences in sequencing depth. Comparing results across batches helps reveal whether an apparent biological group is tied to an experimental procedure.
items.initial_anchor_text: Single-cell assays characterize variability that may be lost during tissue-level averaging. Data analysis must account for technical noise, incomplete sampling, and fluctuations in sequencing depth. Additionally, comparing results across different batches helps determine if an observed biological group is associated with a specific experimental procedure.
